name: irrtoolset
desc: Tools to work with Internet routing policies
why: A door into the Internet Routing Registry and RPSL policy language that quietly steers how the internet routes traffic.

brief.what_it_is: IRRToolSet is a set of command-line tools for working with Internet routing policies, which are stored in Internet Routing Registries (IRRs) in the Routing Policy Specification Language (RPSL). The README says the tools cover automated router configuration, routing policy analysis, and ongoing maintenance of routing information. The README does not describe the inputs and outputs of the individual executables (peval, rpslcheck, rtconfig), so those are not covered here.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the goal is to make routing information more convenient and useful for network engineers by providing tools for automated router configuration, routing policy analysis, and on-going maintenance.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internal mechanism. It says the policies live in IRRs as RPSL text, and the toolset works with them from there.

commands_seen.cmd: $ apt-get install build-essential git libtool bison flex automake autoconf libreadline6-dev
commands_seen.context: Installs the build dependencies on Debian and Ubuntu, which the README says should be sufficient.
First step of the autotools source build, generating the configure script.

brief.install_notes: Source build with autotools. Needs a GNU C++ compiler, libreadline, automake, autoconf, libtool, bison and flex. On Debian/Ubuntu the README gives an apt-get line that includes build-essential, git and libreadline6-dev. No accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration are mentioned. The brew formula is not described in the README.
brief.standout: The README is candid that the project is no longer maintained and points users to BGPQ4 as the better-maintained IRR client. The scout note's claim that the tools 'quietly steer how the internet routes traffic' is not supported by the README, which describes configuration generation and policy analysis tools, not traffic steering.
brief.status: Not actively maintained, according to the README's Status section. I did not find release dates or commit dates on the page, so I cannot say more precisely how quiet it is.
brief.caveats: The README says the project is not actively maintained. It recommends BGPQ4 (https://github.com/bgp/bgpq4) as the maintained alternative. Building from source needs a C++ toolchain plus the autotools chain. The code is under a mix of MIT, RIPE NCC and GNU GPLv2+ licenses, with copyright held by several parties, so check the COPYING file. Bug reports are preferred on GitHub, and discussion happens on a mailing list (irrtoolset@isc.org).
quotes: The IRRToolSet is a set of tools to work with Internet routing policies.
IRRToolSet is not actively maintained. If you're looking for a fast, efficient, well-maintained IRRDB client, BGPQ4 is an excellent choice
IRRToolSet has a long history and several parties hold copyright to various parts of IRRToolSet.
